name: spring-toolcalling
matches: When a tool throws, the exception is wrapped in ToolExecutionException and handed to the ToolExecutionExceptionProcessor:
If you implement your own ToolCallback, throw ToolExecutionException from call() when execution fails — that’s what the processor expects.

With onLimitExceeded(ToolCallLimitBehavior.RETURN_ERROR_RESPONSE), the manager instead skips the call and synthesizes an error ToolResponse — the same mechanism used for ToolExecutionException — so the model is told the limit was reached and the conversation
